summary: Validated with validate --run <run> --submission update48.json returning valid=true after I corrected a typo in the knowledge identifier I was amending, which the first attempt rejected with an unknown knowledge entry diagnostic. This correction sharpens the lease finding's cadence bound. The record said a lease shorter than the typical interval between a leader's contacts with a follower mis-fires, which is directionally right but vague. Since a contact follows either of two independent triggers, the heartbeat loop waiting up to one tenth of the heartbeat timeout or the replication loop re-replicating on the commit timeout, the largest gap between consecutive contacts is bounded by the smaller of those two intervals, not by their sum and not by the heartbeat period. Naming that bound makes the finding checkable against a configuration rather than against an impression while leaving the mechanism, the validation gap and the bounded consequence unchanged; the changed premise field records exactly that substitution. Also carried forward in the same entry is the observation that a configuration with a five millisecond lease and a one second heartbeat timeout is accepted by validation even though the contact bound is around fifty milliseconds with the default commit timeout, so the leader logs that it failed to contact a quorum and steps down repeatedly. Counterevidence is unchanged: the default lease is far above the bound, contact is refreshed by any response including a rejection, the situation is diagnosable from the log line and the transition metric, and nothing was executed because this run had no experiment capacity at any point during my work.
